prompt:
Build a single-file WebGPU "material study" page called "Plush Penguin": editorial studio layout, large italic serif title "Plush / Penguin.", kicker "Material Studies / No. 016", caption "A fluffy egg on two felt feet. It waddles, it toboggans, it falls over — and always gets back up.", live status chip, specimen panel on the right, stats row (Mass, Volume, Steps, Slide in cm), collapsible "Inside the experiment" notes. UI in English, works on mobile.

The toy: a round plush penguin chick — an egg-shaped stuffed body as one SDF meshed with surface nets, a dark cap and back, a pale fluffy face and belly, big glossy safety-glass eyes, a small felt beak, pink cheeks, two flat felt feet. Its flippers are separate cloth pieces (particle cloth sewn to points embedded in the body) that flop, flap and stretch.

Physics: XPBD soft body on a hex lattice (shape-matched cells + tetrahedral volume preservation, live volume readout), skinned to the mesh, standing on a table with Coulomb friction. Locomotion by posture: a weak pull of the whole body toward its rest shape turned to an orientation and carried with its centre of mass, so the stuffing does the moving. Behaviours: Waddle (rocks side to side, lifting each foot and setting it down ahead), Belly slide (a little hop, flops forward onto its tummy and toboggans across the table, then rocks back up), Flap (happy flapping and a couple of hops), Topple (falls onto its back, belly or side and rocks itself upright with an overshoot), Smooth fur, Reset. Finger: it waddles over to your finger; push it and it falls over. Hand: pick it up, squash it, pull a flipper and it comes along.

Fur: real-time shell fur with alpha-to-coverage — long fluffy down on the body, short on the face, combable with a Comb tool (against the grain darker, with it shinier). Sliders: Stuffing, Pile (mm), Table (felt ↔ ice friction, so it slides further on ice). Palettes: Chick, Classic, Little blue. ¼ speed and mesh toggles, Pause. 60 fps.

post.originalText:
It’s just code. So why do I want to hug it? 🐧

GPT-6 Astra vs Claude Opus 5.5 - same prompt, two interactive plush penguins

Astra made a special little guy: big eyes, a cream belly and a personality of his own. Opus is fluffier, but Astra’s penguin is the one I’d actually buy

Both use WebGPU, soft-body physics and brushable fur, each in a single HTML file

Estimated API cost:

Astra: $13.07
Opus: $11.05

Which one would you take home? 👀

sourceMaterials.text:
Plush Penguin — Material Studies / No. 016






Material Studies / No. 016
Sewing a little penguin


Plush /Penguin.
A fluffy egg on two felt feet. It waddles, it toboggans, it falls over — and always gets back up.
PYGOSCELIS / SOFT GOODS
Tabletop specimen, 18 cm
The specimenfig. 016

 Touch
HandFingerComb

 Plumage
ChickClassicLittle blue

 Stuffing 55%softplump

Pile 5.6 mmvelvetdown

Table Feltfeltice


 WaddleBelly slideFlapToppleSmooth furReset
¼ speedMesh
Pause
Perfectly bad at standing still.


Just a little soft around the edges.

Pick it up. Squash the fluff. Tug a flipper.
Drag the empty table to orbit · scroll to zoom.
Mass— g
Volume100.0 %
Steps0
Slide0.0 cm


Inside the experimentOne stuffed shape. An egg-shaped signed distance field becomes a smooth surface-net mesh. Beneath it, hexahedral cells shape-match and tetrahedra preserve volume using an XPBD soft-body solver.
Stuffing does the moving. A gentle posture constraint rotates the rest shape about the measured centre of mass. Alternating felt-foot contacts provide traction. There is no rigid body hiding under the down.
Sewn, not stuck on. Each flipper is a particle-cloth patch. Stretch, shear and bending constraints let it flop; barycentric seams transfer the pull back into the stuffing.
Brushable down. Real-time fur shells use four-sample alpha-to-coverage. The face has shorter pile. Brushing changes the fibre direction, so against-grain strokes look darker and with-grain strokes catch the light.
A slippery slope. Table adjusts Coulomb friction from felt to ice. Slide is measured from the body’s path during the toboggan; volume is the live signed-tetrahedron sum, relative to its rest state.
Native WebGPU · no external assets · adaptive resolution.

STUFFED WITH NUMBERS.
RENDERED WITH A LITTLE AFFECTION.

Fluffing the very important egg…

A little more graphics power.
